title: She's smarter than me!
grammar: Comparative adjectives: -er than and more … than
pair_game: Point at two pictures. Make a sentence: “A is … than B”. Your partner agrees or disagrees. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: -er than
grammar_box.tip: One or two short words: add -er. Long words: use more.

questions: Who is taller, you or your best friend?
Is your brother or sister older than you?
Are you faster than most of your classmates?
Who is smarter in your family?
Is English easier or harder than math for you?
Is your school bigger than your house?
Who is the oldest person in your family?
Are you better at sports than your sister or brother?
What is more interesting for you, TV or books?
Compare yourself and your best friend. Who is taller?
starters: I am taller / My best friend is taller. He/She is … .
Yes, my … is older than me by … years. / No, I am the oldest.
Yes, I am faster than most of them. / No, … is faster than me.
I think … is the smartest in my family, because … .
For me English is easier / harder than maths, because … .
Yes, my school is much bigger. / No, … .
The oldest person in my family is my … . He/She is … .
Yes, I am better at … . / No, my … is better at sports.
I think … is more interesting, because … .
My best friend and I are … . He/She is … than me.
samples: Who is taller, you or your best friend?
My best friend is **taller than** me. He is one metre seventy and I am one metre sixty-two.
Is English easier or harder than math for you?
English is **easier than** maths for me. I like the new words, but the numbers are **more difficult**.
Compare yourself and your best friend. Who is taller?
Jasur is **taller** and **faster than** me, but I am **better** at English. He is also **funnier than** me — he makes the class laugh every day.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: Who is taller — you or your best friend?

game.title: Comparing bingo!
game.rules: Your teacher reads a sentence. If it is true for you, cross the square. Three in a line? Say “Bingo!”
items: My father is taller than me.
I am faster than my friend.
My sister is younger than me.
I am better at English than at maths.
My mother is funnier than my father.
I am older than my cousin.
My friend is smarter than me at maths.
My brother is taller than my mother.
I am the youngest in my family.

mini_talk.title: Me and my family
plan: Say who is older and younger
Say who is funnier or smarter
Say what you are good at
mini_talk.model: There are four people in my family. My brother is three years **older than** me and he is much **taller than** me. My little sister is **younger than** both of us, but she is **funnier than** everybody! My mother says I am **smarter than** my brother at English, but he is **better** at sport. My best friend Jasur is **taller than** me too.

cando: use more … than with long words
